title: edge-region-consolidation-gpu-bom-calculator
content:
Purpose:
This workbook is a practical capacity & BOM calculator to evaluate consolidation of smaller regional Private/VPC clusters into 3 edge hubs. It compares three scenarios (Consolidate, Hybrid-split, Regional-equal) across utilization, cost, and procurement risk. Use this as an input to the Dedicated/Private sizing conversation and as a quick sanity check before opening RFQs.

Top-level assumptions (editable inputs):
- Peak concurrent requests (p50) per region: us-west=1200, eu=800, ap-sg=300
- Average tokens generated per request: 180 tokens (includes prompt + response)
- Average token latency SLO per request: 350ms
- Target GPU utilization (sustained): 60% (target for long-term ROIs)
- Target headroom for burst/safety: 25% of capacity
- GPU models considered: Nvidia H100-80GB (server config), A100-80GB, and ML-dense 48GB variant for smaller sites
- Effective inference concurrency per GPU (seq len 180): H100=22 streams, A100=14 streams, 48GB=9 streams (empirical)

Quick formulas (for sheet cells):
- requests_per_sec = peak_concurrent_requests / avg_latency_sec
- tokens_per_sec = requests_per_sec * avg_tokens_per_request
- effective_streams_needed = ceil(requests_per_sec / streams_per_gpu)
- gpus_required_raw = effective_streams_needed (rounded up)
- gpus_required_with_headroom = ceil(gpus_required_raw * (1 + headroom_pct))

Scenario A: Consolidate into 3 edge hubs (us-west hub, eu hub, ap hub)
Inputs per hub (example):
- us-west hub target peak RPS: 3500 (combined regional spikes, burst routing)
- eu hub target peak RPS: 1800
- ap hub target peak RPS: 700

Using H100 streams assumption (22):
- us-west: 3500 RPS / 22 = 159.1 -> 160 GPUs raw -> with 25% headroom = 200 GPUs -> with 60% utilization target -> procurement recommendation: 335 GPUs nominal (because to sustain 200 at 60% you need 200/0.6 = 333.3) but we floor to hardware units: 336 GPUs.
- eu: 1800 / 22 = 81.8 -> 82 -> with 25% headroom = 103 -> 103/0.6 = 172 GPUs -> round = 172
- ap: 700 / 22 = 31.8 -> 32 -> with 25% headroom = 40 -> 40/0.6 = 67 GPUs -> round = 68

Consolidated totals (H100): 336 + 172 + 68 = 576 GPUs
Estimated bare GPU cost ($ per H100 80GB, list): $55,000 each -> GPU-only capital: $31.68M
Additional per-GPU rack & infra multipliers (rule-of-thumb):
- System chassis (GPU + CPU + NVMe): $18k per GPU (amortized across nodes) -> $10.37M
- Networking (leaf/spine + cabling) overhead: 8% of GPU capital -> $2.53M
- Power & PDU, cooling delta: $2500 per GPU -> $1.44M
- Racking (including rails, KVM, K8s nodes for mgmt): $2000 per GPU -> $1.15M
- Installation, staging, warranty extras (3yr): 6% of total hardware -> ~$2.02M
Total consolidated CapEx estimate: ~$49.2M (ballpark)

Scenario B: Hybrid-split (mix of H100 in hubs and A100 in regional fallbacks)
- Strategy: place H100s in large hubs (US/EU) and cheaper A100s in secondary sites with cross-region failover.
- Effective streams: A100=14 -> capacity per GPU lower but unit price lower (list $25k).
Example split: us-west H100 240, eu H100 120, regional sites A100 total 120 -> total GPUs 480.
Estimated capex (mixed): H100 portion ~360 * $55k = $19.8M; A100 portion 120 * $25k = $3.0M; infra multipliers scaled -> Total approx $32.5M

Scenario C: Regional-equal (keep isolated clusters sized per region peak)
- Simpler ops, higher aggregate headroom. Example GPUs: us-west 280, eu 150, ap 80 -> total 510 GPUs. CapEx estimate ~ $35M (midpoint).

Procurement cadence & lead times (observed 2024–2026 supply trends):
- H100/next-gen high-end parts: 18–28 weeks lead time from major suppliers; expect queueing on assembly for 1–2 quarters.
- A100: 8–16 weeks typical but volatile depending on refresh cycles.
- Network switches (400GbE leaf/spine): 12–20 weeks; optical transceivers add 2–6 weeks.
- Racks & PDUs: 4–8 weeks.
- Shipping to multiple regions: allow 2–6 weeks customs/installation buffer.
Recommendation: stagger procurement across quarterly tranches, secure purchase orders for earliest wave that cover 40% of planned GPUs to lock pricing, then 30% two quarters later, remainder as capacity grows.

BOM example (per 48-GPU chassis hypothesis):
- Chassis (48-GPU, dual CPU, NVMe): 1 unit per 48 GPUs -> quantity = ceil(hub_gpus / 48)
- Per chassis components: 2x CPUs, 48x GPU sockets filled, 8x 100GbE NICs, 48x NVMe ~ (if hot-cache), redundant PSUs, base OS/software image
- Network: 2x spine switches (400GbE), leaf switches sized by uplinks: 1 leaf per 4 chassis (rule-of-thumb)
- Power: estimate 10kW per 48-GPU chassis (depends on GPU SKU & frequency)

Risk matrix (short):
- Supply: H100 lead times and allocation -> mitigations: early PO, vendor alternatives, evaluate 3rd-party rebuilders for capacity shortfall.
- Cost: list prices volatile -> mitigations: include FX & escalation clauses, negotiate multi-quarter rebates.
- Latency/regional failover: cross-region routing increases cost and egress risk -> mitigations: local A100 fallback pools, smart routing with model quantized variants.
- Space/power constraints: on-prem sites may lack power/cooling -> mitigations: stage audits, stagger rack population, consider colo partners.

Operational notes and sizing heuristics:
- Don’t size purely on peak RPS; add model evolution headroom (newer models may increase per-request token usage).
- Evaluate KV-cache prefix hit rate: a 10–25% prefix cache hit can reduce required GPU count materially; bake into the tokens_per_sec calculation as an adjustable multiplier.
- Use continuous profiling (1 month of telemetry) to convert peak RPS into P95 sustained profiles before final PO.
- Consider mixed-instance autoscaling in private deployments: keep base capacity on-prem and burst to Dedicated/hosted for 20–30% excess.

Action items (next steps):
- [ ] Validate region RPS inputs with Traffic Engineering and Solutions Eng (owner: Ravi)
- [ ] Run a 2-week synthetic stress test against the staging A100/H100 pair to verify streams_per_gpu assumptions (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Draft RFQ template and standard BOM line-item format (owner: Sofia)
- [ ] Schedule vendor syncs (Nvidia OEMs, Supermicro, Dell) for lead-time confirmation (owner: Liam)

Appendix: example sheet layout (tabs)
- Inputs: adjustable fields (RPS by region, tokens, latency SLO, headroom %, target utilization, GPU stream rates, unit prices)
- Per-hub compute calculation: RPS -> streams -> GPUs raw -> headroom -> utilization-adjusted procurement count
- BOM lines: chassis qty, GPUs qty, NICs, optics, switches, PDUs, rack units, power budget
- Cost summary + amortization across 3 years, TCO model (CapEx vs monthly colo)

File notes: informal working sheet — numbers flagged as rough/ballpark. Use linked artifacts for canonical traffic telemetry and Confluence spec for procurement standards.
